newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker rates firm as demand rolls forward.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker rates firm as demand rolls forward.

text.p: Prompt dirty tanker rates held steady while rates for early November fixings continued to strengthen as demand rolled forward, brokers said.
They said prompt markets were holding steady, but with most requirements covered they expected rates to start easing.
Further forward, growing tanker avails were also seen putting pressure on rates.
"It depends on what dates you want and whether you're prepared to take older tonnage, but apart from first decade November the market looks generally easier, with demand thin," a broker said.

An active million barrel market out of West Africa to the U.S. Gulf was seen stiring demand for VLCCs. 265,000 tonnes was fixed with options to the U.S. Gulf at a steady W65, UKC at W67.5 and Far East at W50.
On the Suezmax front an Italian refiner was reported paying W115 for early November tonnage but otherwise rates in this period were assessed steady around W107.5.
Further out though, tankers for voyage to the U.S. Gulf after November 15 were seen achieving little better than W100, with tanker avails growing.
